first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both declining, and prior evidence indicates that shorter onboarding improves completion, time-to-value, and early adoption. Promotional pricing addresses the competitive threat but carries a documented 30-day retention penalty, conflicting with the sustainable qualified-revenue objective. Verify the most directly relevant onboarding evidence and the pricing downside before committing.

mid.rationale: Run a standard experiment simplifying onboarding. The verified source showed completion +13%, time-to-value improved by 2.1 days, and 30-day retention +3%, directly addressing both current declines while supporting sustainable revenue. Promotional pricing is rejected despite acquisition gains because verified retention fell 12% and the cohort failed to survive first renewal. A controlled experiment preserves uncertainty about whether the prior onboarding effect will replicate under current conditions.

final2.rationale: Continue with onboarding simplification rather than react with discounting. The verified onboarding experiment improved completion by 13%, shortened time-to-value by 2.1 days, and increased 30-day retention by 3%, directly supporting sustainable qualified revenue. The deeper competitor cut and doubled churn conversations increase urgency but do not overturn verified evidence that a 40% SMB discount reduced 30-day retention by 12% and failed at first renewal. The churn conversations are an important but still preliminary signal, so retain a controlled experiment rather than broaden rollout.
